title: Emil's Sub-max Daily Fingerboard Routine
texts: Sub-maximal isometric hangs - 10 seconds on, 20 off with varied grip positions & feet on the floor at all times

All exercises should be performed using an 18-22mm edge with your feet on the floor at all times.  The intensity of this workout should be very low, such that when you pull, only a small strain is felt in your forearms.

This workout is designed as an injury prevention protocol and a recruitment protocol. It's derived from a study by Keith Baar, who looked at how engineered ligaments were affected by a frequent load and different intensities of said load. This concluded that 10 minutes of low-intensity activity with 6 hours of rest between sessions yielded the best results for healthy tendons. 

This workout is designed to be performed with a 6-hour window between each workout or climbing session. The session should be very light and should not affect climbing performance after 6 hours of rest. This protocol can also be used to recover from an injury, but be extra mindful to keep the load very low. To use this as a recruitment protocol before a trip or competition, you can plan to begin 4-6 weeks before expected peak performance, and the intensity can be kept slightly higher.
